cases.name: zh-tw-paragraph
cases.text: 「如果你只有一天可以待在台南，該怎麼安排？」朋友在捷運上這樣問我。我想了想，建議他一早先去國華街喝碗熱騰騰的牛肉湯，配一碗肉燥飯，再到附近的老店買一杯冬瓜茶。中午可以走到赤崁樓一帶，順路嘗嘗碗粿、蝦捲和鱔魚意麵。台南的小吃偏甜，第一次來的人常常嚇一跳，但吃久了反而會懷念那種味道。許多老店只做早上的生意，有的一天只賣兩百份，賣完就收攤，週末去還得排隊。下午天氣熱，不妨躲進巷弄裡的咖啡店，看看老房子改建的空間怎麼保留原本的木窗與磨石子地板。傍晚再去安平老街散步，買些蜜餞當伴手禮，看夕陽慢慢落進台灣海峽。如果時間還夠，晚上可以去花園夜市逛逛，不過要注意它只在週四、週六和週日營業。可惜台南目前還沒有捷運，移動大多得靠機車或公車；從台北搭高鐵南下大約一個半小時，再轉接駁車進市區。朋友聽完笑著說：「這樣聽起來，一天根本不夠，至少要住三晚吧！」我點點頭，順手把收藏的美食清單傳給他，提醒他記得帶悠遊卡，回台北轉乘捷運時才不會手忙腳亂。

cases.name: ja-paragraph
cases.text: 週末、久しぶりに京都へ出かけました。朝早く新幹線に乗り、駅に着いたらまずコンビニでおにぎりとお茶を買いました。午前中は清水寺を参拝し、坂道の途中にある小さなお店で抹茶ソフトクリームを食べました。昼ごろから雨が降り始めたので、予定を変更して錦市場をぶらぶら歩くことにしました。漬物や湯葉、だし巻き卵など、どれも美味しそうで迷ってしまいます。結局、母へのお土産に京漬物を少しだけ買いました。夕方には鴨川沿いのカフェでコーヒーを飲みながら、スマートフォンで撮った写真を整理しました。帰りの電車ではすっかり疲れて眠ってしまいましたが、とても充実した一日でした。次は紅葉の季節に、友達と一緒にゆっくり旅行したいです。

cases.name: en-paragraph
cases.text: When Maria opened the bakery on 14th Street in 2019, she didn't expect the line to stretch around the block by 7:30 a.m. "People told me sourdough was a fad," she says, laughing, "but we've sold more than 250,000 loaves since then." Her secret isn't complicated: a 36-hour fermentation, flour milled within 120 miles, and a starter she's kept alive for over a decade. Last spring she began posting recipes at https://example.com/recipes?lang=en&page=2, and the site now gets roughly 3,400 visitors a day. It's a small business, but it's hers, and she wouldn't trade it for anything.

policy.notes: Oracle: sentencepiece 0.2.2 on google-gemma2/tokenizer.model, encode(text, add_bos=False, add_eos=False). This is the Gemma 1/2 256k tokenizer that the Vertex AI SDK local tokenizer (vertexai/tokenization/_tokenizer_loading.py) pins, at the same commit and sha256, for gemini-1.0-pro and gemini-1.5-pro/flash; Gemini 2.0+ use the 262k Gemma 3/4 vocabulary instead (google-gemma4). Model proto: model_type=BPE, byte_fallback=true, add_dummy_prefix=false, escape_whitespaces=true, remove_extra_whitespaces=false, split_by_unicode_script=true, split_by_whitespace=true, split_digits=true, normalizer=identity (precompiled_charsmap 0 bytes, so input text is never rewritten except spaces); 256000 pieces: NORMAL 255495, USER_DEFINED 245, BYTE 256 (ids 217..472), CONTROL 3, UNK 1; unk_id=3, bos_id=2, eos_id=1, pad_id=0. Special tokens: SentencePiece has no switch. It never matches CONTROL or UNK pieces in input text ( 0, 1, 2, 3), so a literal '' is encoded as ordinary text. It always matches each of the 245 USER_DEFINED pieces (ids 4..216, 255968..255999) as one atomic token: newline runs, U+2581 runs, tab runs (ids 255969..255998, 2 or more tabs), 100 slots, 50 HTML tags such as and , and [@BOS@] 6, 106, 107, [toxicity=0] 255968. Because the chat-turn markers and are USER_DEFINED, the corpus case special-start-of-turn begins with id 106; that is why specialTokens is user-defined-atomic rather than as-text (asserted). idsWithSpecials is an EMULATION of 'match' semantics: the sentencepiece library has no special-token switch, so tools/oracle/oracles/spm_bpe_ref.py encode(text, match_specials=True) adds the CONTROL and UNK pieces ( 0, 1, 2, 3) to its longest-first USER_DEFINED prefix match, as frozen symbols that map straight to their own ids (never to byte fallback), with the dummy prefix still only at the start of the text. This is the web app's specialTokens: 'match'. Each emulated result must tile the input bytes (a matched piece covers its own text) and must equal the sentencepiece library's ids for the plain text between the matched strings (dummy prefix only on the first stretch) joined by the special ids. It is present only where it differs from ids: special-bos. add_dummy_prefix=false: nothing is prepended, so no token is zero-width, and a leading space is covered by an ordinary U+2581 piece (alone or fused with the following text). Byte spans: research section 5.2 cursor walk. A BYTE piece (ids 217..472, derived from the proto piece types and asserted to equal research sections 3.3/5.2) covers the one byte id - 217; other pieces cover their UTF-8 text, with each U+2581 matching a 0x20 space or a literal U+2581 (E2 96 81) at the cursor. Tab: a single tab has no piece of its own and falls back to BYTE id 226 (<0x09>). Port caveat (research section 5.2): the Hugging Face tokenizer.json for Gemma 1/2 keys byte id 226 as a literal tab character instead of <0x09>, so a JSON-based port must take a BYTE token's value from its id (id - 217), never from its piece string. This fixture reads the .model, where the piece is <0x09>, so it is unaffected. Cross-check: tools/oracle/oracles/spm_bpe_ref.py re-implements SentencePiece BPE encoding in pure Python (no code shared with the library) and must reproduce every case.
